question.text: Which of the following about Incentive Fee CRYSTALLISATION is most consistent with the chapter's treatment of Cat I/II AIFs?

answer.text: Crystallised daily on NAV and paid monthly
Computed and payable after completion of the fund tenure; Cat I/II MAY alternatively pay deal-by-deal after each exit subject to clawback and catch-up
Always paid upfront at fund launch
Crystallised only when LP redeems units

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 6: Incentive Fees for Cat I/II 'are computed and payable to Investment Manager, after completion of the stated fund tenure. Generally, Cat I/II AIFs could also follow a Deal-by-Deal Distribution mechanism, wherein the Incentive Fees are computed and paid after every exit ... subject to clauses such as Clawback Provisions and Catch-up Rates.' **The Trap:** A is Cat III daily-NAV mechanic (excluded from XIX-D); C is absurd; D is open-ended redemption logic — Cat I/II are closed-ended. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers this. XIX-E (Cat III) is where daily NAV + HWM crystallisation is tested. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Deal-by-deal with clawback + 20-30% escrow is today's market-standard compromise in Indian PE/VC. Don't promise LPs end-of-fund carry only — that's LP-friendly but hurts your GP team's cash flow and team retention.
